cases.conclusion: One issuer disclosure distinguishes investment plan, construction, HVM, yield, future ramp and annual capacity. These states must not be collapsed into one expansion flag.
Available capacity can be deliberately reduced/maintained when demand is weak. Lower production/utilization may be an endogenous response to demand, not an independent bearish capacity shock.

falsification: Expansion plan alone is insufficient evidence of effective economic capacity.
Capex amount alone cannot identify growth capacity, timing, yield or utilization.
High utilization is not always favorable; it can represent bottleneck/top-of-cycle pressure.
Low utilization is not always an exogenous negative shock; it may be maintenance, migration or deliberate supply discipline.
Company capacity evidence and industry aggregate capacity evidence are not interchangeable.
No capacity variable receives permanent positive/negative sign before demand, inventory, pricing and margin controls.
